roadmap_item.title: Expand Cassor worker orchestration to Claude Code and Copilot
roadmap_item.description: Extend the Codex-first worker orchestration model with runtime-specific adapters, capability detection, and safe fallbacks for Claude Code and GitHub Copilot.
roadmap_item.rationale: Cross-runtime support follows a proven Codex orchestration contract.

goal: Claude Code and GitHub Copilot receive deterministic Cassor skill adapters that detect available runtime capabilities, preserve local configuration, and fall back safely when worker isolation or model routing is unavailable.

included: Runtime capability status for Codex, Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot
Claude Code adapter assets and deterministic project installation
GitHub Copilot adapter assets and deterministic project installation
Safe fallback guidance when worker or model capabilities are unavailable
Custom configuration preservation, managed-asset protection, and dry-run behavior
Adapter tests, parity checks, documentation, and repository verification
excluded: Remote worker execution or service integrations
Automatic modification of global runtime configuration
Automatic creation of optional custom worker profiles
Claims about worker or token efficiency unavailable to the current runtime

decisions: The portable skill remains canonical; runtime adapters add only runtime-specific capability and fallback guidance.
Capability detection distinguishes supported, configured, and unavailable behavior without treating missing delegation as an installation failure.
Project-scoped installation is the default and preserves unrelated runtime files and custom edits.
Optional worker profiles are not installed by default; adapter assets document how to proceed when a runtime exposes no safe worker mechanism.
The CLI remains authoritative for installation status, managed-file updates, and verification.

acceptance_criteria.title: Capability inspection reports supported, configured, and unavailable runtime features without fabricating worker or model support.
Claude Code and Copilot project installations include deterministic adapter guidance alongside the canonical portable skill.
Install, update, dry-run, and status flows preserve unrelated runtime configuration and reject unmanaged destination conflicts.
When worker isolation or explicit model routing is unavailable, adapters direct the runtime to a safe single-agent fallback while retaining approval and verification gates.
Adapter assets remain aligned with the portable skill and full repository tests, vet, site build, and cassor check pass.

constraints: Preserve the existing portable skill and installer manifest contract.
Keep all runtime-specific behavior explicit and testable from the current Go CLI.
Do not overwrite user-authored runtime configuration or unrelated instructions.
Do not persist worker transcripts, hidden reasoning, or unavailable telemetry.

tasks.title: Add runtime capability inspection and adapter asset model
tasks.description: Extend configuration and skill services with explicit runtime capability status, agent-specific embedded assets, and stable adapter metadata without changing the portable authority contract.

tasks.title: Implement Claude Code adapter installation and fallback guidance
tasks.description: Add Claude-specific project adapter guidance, capability-safe fallback rules, and installer coverage that preserves custom files and avoids global configuration writes.

tasks.title: Implement Copilot adapter installation and fallback guidance
tasks.description: Add Copilot-specific project adapter guidance, optional capability handling, and installer coverage for canonical skill parity and unmanaged destination protection.

tasks.title: Verify cross-runtime parity and document safe operation
tasks.description: Exercise capability status, dry-run and update flows, inspect all installed assets, document adapter boundaries, rebuild the roadmap, and confirm repository invariants.

risks: Runtime-specific asset placement may drift from the canonical portable skill unless embedded parity tests compare shared files.
Installed runtime directories may contain user-authored configuration; managed-file hashes must continue to gate updates and uninstalls.
Claude Code and Copilot capability surfaces vary by installation and version, so the adapter must report unknown capabilities as unavailable rather than infer support.
